from.place: proof of the tensor irreducibility lemma: reduction by the limit argument to domains of finite type over the algebraically closed field

title: Finite-type reduction for tensor products
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension] and let $R$, $S$ be $k$-algebras; call a ring reduced if it has no nonzero nilpotent elements, and a $k$-subalgebra finitely generated if it is generated as a $k$-algebra by finitely many elements. (1) If $R\otimes_kS$ is not reduced, then there are finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $R'\subset R$ and $S'\subset S$ such that $R'\otimes_kS'$ is not reduced. (2) If $R\otimes_kS$ contains a nonzero zero-divisor, then there are finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $R'\subset R$ and $S'\subset S$ such that $R'\otimes_kS'$ contains a nonzero zero-divisor.

proof.text: For the reducedness clause, argue contrapositively. If every pair of finitely generated subalgebras has reduced tensor product, apply Mathlib IsReduced.tensorProduct_of_flat_of_forall_fg first to R with a fixed finitely generated S-stage, then to S. Use Algebra.TensorProduct.comm and isReduced_of_injective to reverse factors between the applications. Vector spaces are free and hence flat; Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType converts the finiteness conditions. This proves R tensor_k S reduced, contradicting the hypothesis.

For the zero-divisor clause, lift each of x and y in R tensor_k S using Mathlib exists_fg_and_mem_baseChange. Take the supremum of the two finitely generated S-subalgebras; Subalgebra.FG.sup proves that it is finitely generated. Map the representatives into this common stage using Subalgebra.inclusion. Algebra.TensorProduct.map_id_comp and Subalgebra.val_comp_inclusion verify that their images are x and y. This is the private proved helper lift_pair_right.

The tensor inclusion of the common stage is injective by Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap, since R is a vector space over k. Nonzeroness follows from the nonzero images; injectivity and preservation of multiplication imply that the representatives have product zero. This is zero_divisors_right. Tensor symmetry transports zero-divisor witnesses (zero_divisors_comm). Apply the one-sided descent first to S tensor_k R and then to R-prime tensor_k S, obtaining the required finitely generated subalgebras in both factors. Convert FG to FiniteType with Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType.

lean.statement: theorem tensor_finite_type_limit (k : Type u) [Field k] (R : Type v) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (S : Type w) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] : (¬ IsReduced (R ⊗[k] S) → ∃ (R' : Subalgebra k R) (S' : Subalgebra k S), Algebra.FiniteType k R' ∧ Algebra.FiniteType k S' ∧ ¬ IsReduced (R' ⊗[k] S')) ∧ ((∃ x y : R ⊗[k] S, x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ x * y = 0) → ∃ (R' : Subalgebra k R) (S' : Subalgebra k S), Algebra.FiniteType k R' ∧ Algebra.FiniteType k S' ∧ ∃ x y : R' ⊗[k] S', x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ x * y = 0)
